cases.name: Yuliana Quintana
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Yuliana era una mujer hermosa llena de vida, que donde quiera que fuera iluminaba el lugar con su sonrisa. Ella siempre le dedicaba su tiempo a sus hijas y a estar con sus hermanos. Le gustaba pasar su tiempo organizando y limpiando, eso lo saco de su mama.

A Yuliana la recordaremos como una persona alegre, amorosa, y valiente. Que todavía le faltaban muchos sueños que realizar. La extrañaremos y siempre estará en nuestro corazón.

She leaves behind to cherish her memory, her loving parents, Gudelia and Jose Quintana; daughters, Natalie and Leahnie; siblings, Jose, Liseth, Omar, Julián, Yonic and Melisa; as well as many other family members and friends who loved her and will miss her dearly.

Yuliana was a beautiful woman full of life and she lit up the room with her smile as soon as she walked in. She always prioritized her time with her girls and with her siblings. She got her love of organizing and cleaning from her mom and was frequently doing one or the other."



She will be remembered as someone who was joyful, loving, and courageous. She had so many unfulfilled dreams left to accomplish. We will miss her always and she will forever remain in our hearts.

cases.name: Dr. Talat Jehan Khan
cases.about:
She was a pediatrician. “She was honestly the most loving and kind person,” Khan’s niece Mahnoor Mangrio said Monday. “I know everyone says that, but she had no bad bone in her body. We have always said she was the most innocent soul in our family. She is such an amazing mother, her whole life revolved around her kids.” Mangrio said Khan moved to Conroe in July from Seattle with her daughter. According to her LinkedIn profile, Khan worked at Sea Mar Community Health Centers in Seattle for 15 years before taking the position with Texas Children’s Pediatrics in Conroe. Mangrio said Khan was passionate about her work as a pediatrician. “The last text I have from her was her saying how happy she was to get to do what she loves,” Mangrio said.
Khan, Mangrio said, was strong in her faith and always willing to help other family members. “She always supported me,” Mangrio said. “I could go to her with anything. There hasn’t been a step in my life where she hasn’t been there for me.”

cases.name: Floris Lee “Flo” Wolford
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "Flo was a woman of strength, honesty, and unwavering conviction. She was known for her direct nature—never afraid to tell it like it is—yet always motivated by a deep desire to uplift and inspire others. Her words carried wisdom, encouragement, and a belief in the potential of those around her, especially when it came to the value of education.

Her greatest passion was her career in education, where she dedicated over 30 years of service in Special Education within school districts in Texas and Las Vegas. Flo made a lasting impact on countless students and families, advocating tirelessly for children with special needs. She was also a devoted advocate for autism awareness and supported initiatives for battered women, extending her compassion beyond the classroom.

A woman of strong Christian faith, Flo lived her life guided by her beliefs, offering love, resilience, and grace to those who knew her. In her leisure time, she found joy in interior decorating and cherished every moment spent with her family, whom she loved deeply.

Floris Lee Wolford leaves behind a legacy of strength, service, and inspiration that will continue to live on in the hearts of all who knew and loved her."
